newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Serial System to expand regionally, eye on China.
newsitem.headline: Serial System to expand regionally, eye on China.

text.p: Electronic components distributor Serial System Pte Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to expand in lucrative Asian markets, especially Taiwan and China, to boost earning potential over the next five years.

"China is one of the biggest markets in the Asia Pacific. It is a natural migration for any company to seek expansion there," Eddie Chng, vice president and chief operating officer said at a briefing on the company's initial public offering (IPO).
Apart from its office in Chengdu, in Sichuan province, it will be setting up an office in Hong Kong this year to manage its growing Chinese business, Chng said.
The group also plans to set up offices in Shenzhen, Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou.
Negotiations were currently underway for ventures in India and Britain, he said, but declined to give details.

Serial System said it would offer 37 million shares for listing on Singapore's second board, SESDAQ. Of those, 27.75 million shares would be offered to the public and 9.25 million would be placed out to institutions.
"Demand exceeds supply. It is over subscribed," Lim Koong Ngee, vice president corporate finance of United Overseas Bank, lead manager for the IPO, said of the private placement.
The public tranche was offered at Singapore $0.58 and the private tranche at $0.60.
The offer represents 19 percent of the company's enlarged share capital of 187.5 million shares and the listing aims to raise S$12.2 million in funds for expansion.
"Of the proceeds, $5.5 million would be used to finance our operations in Taiwan," Chng said.
About two-thirds of Serial System's revenue is generated in Singapore, but the group would like to see 60 percent come from overseas markets in three to five years, he said.
The group carries more than 1,500 products from 33 principals and distributes them to five major sectors such as data storage, computers, telecommunications and consumer electronics.
Some of its main principals are multinationals like Texas Instruments, IBM, United MicroElectronics Corp and AT&T.
Derek Goh, the president and chief executive officer who founded the company in 1988, said it provided value-added integrated circuit design and applications to customised components.
"The group is able to customise off-the-shelf products as well as design integrated circuits to meet customers' specific needs,' Goh said.
Serial System recorded a group net profit of S$7.4 million for the financial year ended June 30, 1996 on a turnover of S$184.3 million.
The company said in a statement it aimed to achieve approximately S$1 billion in sales revenue within the next five to 10 years.
